themes.label: Functional mean-change model and hypothesis setup
themes.need: Someone wanting to test for a change in the mean function of a sequence of functional (curve) observations needs the functional mean-change model (eq. 1.1-1.2) and the null (no change) vs. alternative (one change at unknown time) hypothesis formulation.

themes.label: Karhunen-Loeve decomposition and estimated covariance operator
themes.need: Someone wanting to reduce an infinite-dimensional functional-data change-point problem to a tractable finite-dimensional one needs the Karhunen-Loeve/Mercer decomposition of the covariance operator and its empirical (estimated) counterpart (eq. 1.3-1.4).

themes.label: Berkes et al. test statistic and Theorem 1.1
themes.need: Someone wanting to first test whether a change exists before estimating its location needs the Berkes et al. change-detection test statistic S_n,d projected onto the leading estimated eigenfunctions, and Theorem 1.1's asymptotic null distribution.

themes.label: Change-point estimator and its limit distribution
themes.need: Someone wanting to estimate where a detected mean change occurred and build confidence intervals for the break date needs the change-point estimator definition (eq. 2.1) with its covariance-kernel/eigenfunction characterization (Proposition 2.1), together with Theorems 2.1-2.2 giving the estimator's limit law both when the mean shift stays fixed and when it shrinks to zero as the sample size grows.

themes.label: Simulation summary statistics for the change-point estimator
themes.need: Someone wanting numerical evidence on the change-point estimator's finite-sample accuracy needs Table 1's simulation summary statistics (bias, spread) across designs.

themes.label: Finite-sample simulation design and results
themes.need: Someone wanting to replicate or interpret the finite-sample simulation study needs the data-generating design (functional-data model, change-magnitude and location settings) and the resulting assessment of the estimator's performance.

themes.label: Proof preliminaries: decomposition of R_n(k)
themes.need: Someone wanting to verify the theorems needs the preliminary decomposition of the process R_n(k) (eq. 4.1-4.2) that the subsequent proofs of Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 build on.

themes.label: Proof of Theorem 2.1
themes.need: Someone wanting to verify the limit distribution under a constant mean shift needs the full proof of Theorem 2.1, including Lemmas 4.1-4.2.

themes.label: Proof of Theorem 2.2
themes.need: Someone wanting to verify the limit distribution under a vanishing mean shift needs the full proof of Theorem 2.2, including Lemmas 4.3-4.4.

themes.label: Appendix A: verification of eq. 4.4
themes.need: Someone wanting the technical verification of an intermediate identity used in the main proofs needs Appendix A's derivation of eq. 4.4, including Lemmas A.1-A.3.

themes.label: Appendix B: verification of eq. 4.7
themes.need: Someone wanting the technical verification of another intermediate identity used in the main proofs needs Appendix B's derivation of eq. 4.7, including Lemmas B.1-B.3.
